# Release protocol test vectors

`decisions.json` and `manifests.json` are copied from
[`anomalyco/release`](https://github.com/anomalyco/release) `test-vectors/` (2026-11-07). They are the service's client
decision vectors: every client must reproduce `src/protocol/decide.ts`, and `test/release-vectors.test.ts` runs all of
them against `cli/src/update/release-service.ts`.

When the release repo changes the rules or the vectors (`bun run vectors` there), copy both files here in the same
change. `semver.json` is not needed: clients never order versions.

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [dev]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  check:
    name: Typecheck, build and test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # Bun from package.json's packageManager field.
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        with:
          bun-version-file: package.json

      # The MCP server and relay run under Node (cli/package.json engines), and the execute sandbox tests run in it too.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Install (extension)
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Install (cli)
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
        working-directory: cli

      - name: Typecheck (extension)
        run: bun run typecheck

      - name: Typecheck (cli)
        run: bun run typecheck
        working-directory: cli

      - name: Build (extension)
        run: bun run build

      - name: Build (cli)
        run: bun build.ts
        working-directory: cli

      - name: Test (extension)
        run: bun test ./test

      - name: Test (cli)
        run: bun run test
        working-directory: cli

      # The store zip and npm tarball the release workflow would build, with its artifact checks (permission allowlist,
      # no key, pairing code, source maps or test hooks), so a problem shows up on the PR rather than at release time.
      - name: Release artifacts check
        run: bun run release:check

      # The release builds a binary per platform (cli/script/compile.ts); this host's one shows a compile break early.
      - name: Compile and pack the linux-x64 binary
        working-directory: cli
        run: |
          bun script/compile.ts linux-x64
          ./dist-bin/browse-linux-x64/bin/browse --version
          bun script/pack.ts

      # The scripts the release jobs that hold secrets run (.github/release/); shellcheck comes with the runner image.
      - name: Shellcheck release scripts
        run: shellcheck -x .github/release/*.sh

  browser:
    name: Execute sandbox in headless Chromium (optional)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    # Informational: a real-browser check of the execute sandbox; a failure here doesn't fail CI.
    continue-on-error: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        with:
          bun-version-file: package.json

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Install (extension)
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Install (cli)
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
        working-directory: cli

      - name: Build (extension)
        run: bun run build

      - name: Build (cli)
        run: bun build.ts
        working-directory: cli

      # The Chromium the pinned patchright-core expects, with its system libraries.
      - name: Install Chromium
        run: node node_modules/patchright-core/cli.js install --with-deps --no-shell chromium
        working-directory: cli

      - name: Execute sandbox browser harness
        run: node --no-warnings test/execute-realm-browser.ts
        working-directory: cli

{
  "$comment": "What the store zip and the npm package's extension may ask the browser for. scripts/check-artifacts.ts fails the release when the built manifest differs from this in either direction, so a new permission is a reviewed change here (and a new justification in store/listing.md), never a side effect.",
  "permissions": [
    "alarms",
    "debugger",
    "notifications",
    "offscreen",
    "scripting",
    "storage",
    "tabCapture",
    "tabGroups",
    "tabs",
    "webNavigation"
  ],
  "optional_permissions": [],
  "host_permissions": ["<all_urls>"],
  "optional_host_permissions": [],
  "content_scripts": [],
  "web_accessible_resources": [],
  "externally_connectable": null
}

# browse privacy policy

_Last updated: October 28, 2026_

browse is a browser extension that lets OpenCode, running on your own computer, use your browser. This policy explains what it handles and where that goes.

## What the extension handles
- **Page content, screenshots, network traffic, and actions** in tabs an agent opened, or tabs you let agents use with the toolbar button.
- **Recordings** of a tab, when you ask an agent for one.
- Which tabs agents opened, kept in your browser's extension storage so idle ones can be closed.
- The pairing code you enter on the status page (or that the installer put in the extension's folder), and the key the OpenCode relay gives this browser in exchange for it, kept in extension storage. The key is never sent anywhere: the extension only proves it holds it.
- A system notification, shown only when an agent needs you while it records a tab.
- **Site secrets** you choose to store with the `browse secrets add` command (a password, key or one-time-code seed, and the sites it may be typed on). They stay in a file on your computer that only your user account can read, and are typed only into fields on those sites. The extension never stores them; they are never sent anywhere except into the page you allowed, and your agent never receives them.

## Where it goes
- To **the OpenCode tools on your computer**, over a local connection (127.0.0.1). The extension only obeys a relay that proves it holds this browser's key, and the relay only answers programs that hold its token, a file only your user account can read.
- OpenCode may send it to the AI model provider **you** configured in OpenCode, under that provider's terms. The extension itself doesn't choose or contact any provider.

Anomaly, the maker of OpenCode, doesn't run a server for this extension and doesn't receive, sell, or share your data. There's no analytics or tracking.

## Your choices
- Agents can't use your tabs unless you click the toolbar button on them. Click again to take a tab back.
- Remove the extension and run `browse uninstall` (`npx @opencode/browse uninstall` if you installed with npx, `node cli/dist/cli.mjs uninstall` from a checkout) to delete everything it set up.

## Contact
Questions: open an issue at https://github.com/anomalyco/browse.

# Stress testing browse

Scripts that stress browse end to end on a real, headed Chrome: a scenario suite, a soak with chaos, a fuzzer and a
smoke test. They run on a disposable Linux box (we use the exe.dev VM `browse-stress.exe.xyz`), never on a machine
whose browser or relay someone uses.

## The box

`exe/provision.sh` sets up an Ubuntu 24.04 box and is safe to re-run:

- Node 24 (in `/usr/local`), Bun (the `packageManager` version), Xvfb + fluxbox, Noto fonts (CJK, emoji), ffmpeg,
  x11vnc + noVNC, and Chrome for Testing stable (`~/chrome-for-testing/current`).
- `~/browse`: a clone of this repo, built and paired with `bun run setup`.
- systemd units (`exe/units/`): `browse-xvfb` (display `:99`), `browse-wm`, `browse-chrome` (headed Chrome with the
  extension, restarted on crash), `browse-vnc` (localhost only) and `browse-novnc` (port 8000).
- The relay is not a service: like on a laptop, any CLI or MCP call starts it on `127.0.0.1:19988`.

Chrome's flags are in `exe/chrome.sh`. The profile is `~/stress-profile` with developer mode on (browse's
`install`/`update` reload the extension, and Chrome disables reloaded unpacked extensions while developer mode is
off). Chrome also listens on `127.0.0.1:9222` (`--remote-debugging-port`): **that port is for the harness only**, to
click handoff cards like a person, stop the extension's service worker and count tabs, groups and debugger
attachments. browse never uses it.

Watch the browser at <https://browse-stress.exe.xyz/vnc.html> (exe.dev's proxy, private to people with access to the
VM; keep it private). Click **Connect**; no VNC password, the proxy is the gate.

```sh
wssh browse-stress.exe.xyz                                 # shell (wssh: ssh with the work key)
wssh browse-stress.exe.xyz 'node ~/browse/cli/dist/cli.mjs status'
wssh browse-stress.exe.xyz 'sudo systemctl restart browse-chrome'
stress/exe/deploy.sh                                       # copy this working tree to the box, rebuild, restart the relay
```

`deploy.sh` rsyncs uncommitted work too (nothing is pushed), keeping the box's `.git`, `node_modules`, builds and
pairing code.

## Canary

`bash stress/exe/provision.sh --canary-only` adds the release lane to a provisioned box without rebuilding its checkout
or restarting `browse-chrome`. User `canary` installs the published dev binary via the real Bash installer. Its headed
Chrome for Testing uses the installer's checksum-verified dev zip, a private Xvfb and relay `:19770`; the kernel blocks
that user's access to `:19988`. Every ~5 min the daemon checks npm. It observes the live relay **and loaded extension**
switching, allows an idle update window, and flags and forces `browse update` after an hour. Each build gets core
scenarios and 30 min of chaos. At ~03:00 local time (or next idle slot) it runs 60 min of all chaos, 15 min of fuzz,
an npx MCP smoke, then 30 min of two-browser affinity checks if Brave installed. Network faults affect only `canary`;
the toolbar fault uses a real keyboard shortcut. Runs are serial. Between them it submits a fixture form, occasionally
visits example.com, samples RSS/fds/tabs and leaves quiet time before reconnecting. At 6 min down it tries a user relay
restart; at 30 min it restarts its own browser and forces the relay restart. Both actions are recorded.

```sh
sudo -Hu canary /usr/local/bin/node /opt/browse-canary/stress/canary/report.ts   # last 24 h + 7 d
sudo systemctl stop browse-canary     # pause (disable --now to keep paused after reboot); start to resume
```

History and private run folders (`result.json`, `summary.md`, `run.log` and the harness artifacts) live under
`/home/canary/canary`. Optional: set `CANARY_SLACK_WEBHOOK` in root-only `/etc/browse-canary-alerts.env` and restart
`browse-canary`; unset means journal only. Alerts link to the host with the run path (or `CANARY_RESULTS_URL/<run>/`
if an existing private artifact viewer is configured). No success alerts. The canary doesn't publish results.

## Runners

All of them run on the box from `~/browse`, write JSONL plus a `summary.md` under `~/stress-results/<time>-<kind>/`
and exit non-zero when something failed.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `node stress/smoke.ts` | One MCP stdio session: initialize, tools/list, status, navigate, snapshot, fill, click, screenshot, network capture, recording, session_delete |
| `node stress/run-scenarios.ts [--only a,b] [--tag core] [--repeat N]` | The scenario suite (`scenarios.ts`) once, serially, a fresh session per scenario |
| `node stress/soak.ts [--workers 8] [--minutes 60] [--chaos-every 120] [--chaos a,b]` | N agents loop scenarios and real sites while chaos hits; metrics every 30 s |
| `node stress/fuzz.ts [--minutes 15] [--seed N]` | Malformed and hostile input at the HTTP API, CDP WebSocket, /extension and MCP tools |
| `bash stress/run-all.sh [soakMinutes] [fuzzMinutes]` | All of the above in order (run it in tmux) |

```sh
wssh browse-stress.exe.xyz "tmux new -d -s stress 'bash ~/browse/stress/run-all.sh 60 15 2>&1 | tee ~/stress-results/run-all.log'"
rsync -az -e wssh browse-stress.exe.xyz:stress-results/ /tmp/browse-stress-results/   # fetch results
```

Type-check the runners with `cli/node_modules/.bin/tsgo --noEmit -p stress/tsconfig.json` (they run with Node's type
stripping, no build step).

The scenarios serve a fixture site on `127.0.0.1:4510` (and `localhost:4510` as a second origin). Add a scenario by
appending to `scenarios` in `scenarios.ts`; tag it `soak` if it's safe to run beside other agents.

**Soak chaos events:** `relay-kill9` (kill -9; the next call restarts it), `sw-stop` (terminates the extension's
service worker), `close-agent-tabs`, `close-windows`, `chrome-restart`, `network-drop` (iptables drops ports 80, 443
and 53 for 10 to 25 s), `session-delete` (mid-task), `mcp-kill` (an agent's MCP server dies), `tabs-cleanup`,
`toolbar-stop` (the user clicks the toolbar button on an agent's tab, the kill switch). After each one a probe session
must run an execute within `--recovery-bound` seconds. Tasks overlapping a chaos window are left out of the success
rate. Pass criteria: calm success rate, every event recovered, no stuck workers, no relay restarts that chaos didn't
cause, bounded growth (relay RSS, fds, tabs per hour, fitted after a 5-minute warm-up), every tab a session holds
tracked for idle cleanup throughout, and no leaked tabs after the run (neither held by a session nor a window's active
tab).

`toolbar-stop` clicks through a test hook the extension has only when built with `OPENCODE_BROWSER_TEST_HOOKS=1`
(`exe/deploy.sh` builds it that way; release builds compile the hook out). It lives in the service worker's globals,
which the harness reaches over the debugging port; pages can't.

**Fuzz checks:** the relay never restarts or stops answering `/version`, nothing but `/` and `/version` answers without
the token, foreign `Host` headers and non-extension origins are refused, an unpaired `/extension` client never
displaces the real extension, and the MCP server never exits on bad input.

## Installed artifacts (what users run)

`installed.ts` drives browse the way a user has it, not the checkout: the binary the curl installer put in a throwaway
`$HOME` (or the npm shim), a headed Chrome for Testing with the **release zip** as the store extension, paired through
install's link or by typing the code into the settings page. Each scenario injects one fault a user meets and records how
long browse took to work again and whether the user had to do anything:

```sh
stress/exe/installed-setup.sh curl            # curl installer into ~/u/home-curl
stress/exe/installed-setup.sh curl 0.0.6 old  # a pinned version into ~/u/home-curl-old
stress/exe/installed-setup.sh npm             # npm installer into ~/u/home-npm
node stress/installed.ts [--user curl] [--port 19988] [--debug-port 9222] [--extension ~/u/ext-0.0.8-store] [--only a,b]
```

The extension folders under `~/u/ext-*` are the release zips with the store's public key added to `manifest.json`, so
loaded unpacked they get the store id (`mfnicocicmmlkpjnaffgihfjhdgjkdjg`), which is the only store origin the relay
accepts. Get the key from the store's CRX header (`clients2.google.com/service/update2/crx?…x=id%3D<id>%26uc`,
CRX3 `sha256_with_rsa.public_key`). Several users can run side by side on different relay ports and debugging ports.

Scenarios: `first-pairing`, `repair-after-revoke`, `relay-kill9`, `relay-restart`, `chrome-restart`, `chrome-crash`,
`sw-stop`, `extension-reload`, `extension-update` (old build in, reload, new build in, reload), `sleep` (relay and
browser SIGSTOPped), `sleep-chrome-only`, `sleep-relay-only`, `network-drop` (the relay port), `two-browsers`,
`remote-pairing` (`install --remote`, a second profile pairs at the box's network address), `npm-to-binary` (the curl
installer over an npm install), `many-agents`, `agents-die`, `idle`. The long ones (`sleep-*`, `idle`, `remote-pairing`,
`npm-to-binary`, `repair-after-revoke`) run only with `--only`.

**Soak chaos events added for connection stress:** `relay-freeze` and `chrome-freeze` (SIGSTOP for 25 to 45 s, the
machine sleeping), `relay-port-drop` (iptables drops the relay's port, a VPN flap) and `extension-reload`. Run these
on a disposable Linux stress VM; the canary retains its original chaos set and restricted network helper.

## Driving the box from a Mac

The MCP server can run on the box over SSH, so an agent on a Mac drives the box's browser:

```sh
node stress/smoke.ts --remote browse-stress.exe.xyz   # initialize, tools/list, status through wssh
```

An opencode MCP server entry for it (add it yourself; nothing here edits your config):

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "browse-stress": {
        "type": "local",
        "command": ["wssh", "browse-stress.exe.xyz", "/usr/local/bin/node", "/home/exedev/browse/cli/dist/cli.mjs", "mcp"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Use the full `/usr/local/bin/node` path: exe.dev's SSH `PATH` lists `/usr/local/bin` last.

## Stealth on a real Mac (manual, never CI)

The box above measures robustness, not stealth: Linux, Xvfb and Chrome for Testing look nothing like a user's
browser. `stress/stealth/run.ts` measures what sites can tell about browse on a real browser (Chrome or Helium on a
Mac). It opens public detector sites, so it never runs in CI, isn't part of `run-all.sh`, and should run only when
someone starts it.

```sh
cd cli && bun build.ts && cd ..                      # the runner uses this checkout's cli/dist/cli.mjs
node stress/stealth/run.ts                           # local probe, then every detector site
node stress/stealth/run.ts --probe-only              # only the local probe (no public sites)
node stress/stealth/run.ts --sites sannysoft,creepjs --wait-ms 10000
node stress/stealth/run.ts --sites-file my-sites.json --out /tmp/stealth-run
```

It drives browse the way an agent does, through the MCP server (`session_new`, then `execute` with `page.mouse`,
`page.click` and `page.keyboard`, so human-like input applies), against whichever relay `OPENCODE_BROWSER_HOME` and
`OPENCODE_BROWSER_PORT` select. Prefer a separate browser profile paired to its own relay (a different
`OPENCODE_BROWSER_HOME` and `OPENCODE_BROWSER_PORT`) over your everyday one, and note the browser version, macOS
version and network. Report a clean-profile run and a warm-profile run separately: clearance cookies change verdicts.

- **Local probe** (`stress/stealth/probe.html` and `snapshot.js`, served on `127.0.0.1`): records, while browse moves,
  hovers, clicks, types and scrolls: `screenX`/`screenY` against `clientX`/`clientY` (Chromium bug 40280325),
  `getCoalescedEvents()`/`getPredictedEvents()` emptiness, `isTrusted`, `movementX/Y`, click `detail`, inter-event
  timing and key dwell distributions; `nextHopProtocol` of the document against its subresources (document
  interception); navigator, User-Agent Client Hints, platform, `hardwareConcurrency`, `deviceMemory`, languages and
  timezone in the window against dedicated, shared and service workers; outer against inner window size, focus and
  visibility over the run; `Function.prototype.toString` of common APIs; automation globals, extra globals, `<html>`
  attributes and DOM nodes the page didn't add; main-world calls with foreign stacks; whether a console listener
  serialized an `Error` (the `Runtime.enable` tell); and the stack a main-world `page.evaluate` shows.
- **Detector sites** (`--sites` ids): `sannysoft` (bot.sannysoft.com), `browserscan` (browserscan.net/bot-detection),
  `creepjs`, `rebrowser` (bot-detector.rebrowser.net), `deviceandbrowserinfo` (are_you_a_bot), `pixelscan`,
  `fingerprint-demo` (demo.fingerprint.com bot firewall) and `recaptcha-v3` (antcpt.com score detector). Each gets a
  screenshot, a best-effort verdict read from the page (sites change; the screenshot is the ground truth) and any
  `aftermath.challenge` execute saw. `--sites-file` takes `[{ "id", "url", "waitMs"?, "extract"? }]`, where `extract`
  is the body of an async function run in the page that returns the verdict.

Results go to `~/stress-results/<time>-stealth/` (or `--out`): `summary.md`, `results.json`, `probe.json` and one PNG
per page. Keep them private: they describe the machine and browser.

export * as AuthenticatedOrigin from "./opencode-browser-client.ts"
export * as OpenCodeBrowserClient from "./opencode-browser-client.ts"
export * as SecretProfile from "./secret-profile.ts"

import * as AuthProfile from "./auth/profile.ts"

export type Summary = AuthProfile.AuthProfileSummary
export type RunResult = AuthProfile.AuthRunResult
export type RunOptions = AuthProfile.AuthRunOptions
export type StatusOptions = AuthProfile.AuthProfileOptions
export type Error = AuthProfile.AuthProfileError
export const Error = AuthProfile.AuthProfileError

/** Return profile metadata without revealing credential values. */
export const status = AuthProfile.status

/**
 * Run a trusted credential-bearing worker with profile slots injected as BC_SECRET_N.
 * Known values are redacted from bounded stdout and stderr before they return.
 */
export const run = AuthProfile.run

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copies this working tree (committed or not) to the box and rebuilds there, for testing fixes without pushing.
#   stress/exe/deploy.sh [host]        # default host: browse-stress.exe.xyz, reached with `wssh`
# Leaves the box's .git, node_modules, builds and pairing code alone, restarts the relay on the new build and reloads
# the extension. The extension is built with the harness's test hooks (OPENCODE_BROWSER_TEST_HOOKS=1).
set -euo pipefail
HOST="${1:-browse-stress.exe.xyz}"
SSH="${BROWSE_STRESS_SSH:-wssh}"
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."
rsync -az --delete -e "$SSH" \
  --exclude .git --exclude node_modules --exclude dist --exclude cli/dist --exclude cli/extension \
  --exclude release --exclude relay-pairing.json --exclude stress-results \
  ./ "$HOST:browse/"
"$SSH" "$HOST" 'bash -se' <<'REMOTE'
set -uo pipefail
export PATH=/usr/local/bin:$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH OPENCODE_BROWSER_UPDATE_CHECK=0
cd ~/browse
(cd cli && OPENCODE_BROWSER_TEST_HOOKS=1 bun build.ts)
# Restart first: `pair` runs `session list`, which refuses a relay of another build (lifecycle.ts relayBuildProblem).
node cli/dist/cli.mjs relay restart --force   # a stress box: nothing a fuzz run left (flight recorders) is worth keeping
# Feed the unpacked extension a real one-time code without running install (which edits the user's MCP config).
umask 077
(node cli/dist/cli.mjs pair --wait-seconds 1 || true) | jq -Rse '{code: capture("Pairing code: (?<code>[0-9A-Z]{4}-[0-9A-Z]{4})").code}' > dist/relay-pairing.json
sudo -n systemctl restart browse-chrome
# Restarting Chrome alone can restore the previous unpacked service worker from the profile's cache.
node --input-type=module <<'JS'
import { BrowserCdp } from './stress/lib/cdp.ts'
import { sleep } from './stress/lib/env.ts'
for (let i = 0; i < 30; i++) {
  const cdp = await BrowserCdp.connect().catch(() => undefined)
  try {
    const scheduled = await cdp?.evalInExtension('typeof setTimeout === "function" && typeof chrome?.runtime?.reload === "function" && !!setTimeout(() => chrome.runtime.reload(), 100)').catch(() => false)
    if (scheduled) break
  } finally { cdp?.close() }
  await sleep(1000)
}
JS
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  if node cli/dist/cli.mjs status --json | jq -e --slurpfile expected dist/build.json '
    select(.relay.running and (.relay.stale == false) and .extension.connected and .extension.build == $expected[0].build)
    | {relay: .relay, extension: (.extension | {connected, version, build, protocolVersion})}'; then exit 0; fi
  sleep 1
done
echo 'Timed out waiting for the new extension build to connect' >&2
exit 1
REMOTE
